key_insight: Universal YOCO (YOCO-U) fuses the YOCO decoder-decoder layout with recursive computation to enable efficient test-time depth scaling — significantly reducing KV-cache growth and per-step overhead while preserving (or improving) reasoning capacity.
problem_solved: Standard Transformer inference loops incur high computational overhead and a KV cache that grows with model depth, making test-time depth scaling expensive or infeasible for improving reasoning and agentic behavior.
method: Integrate the YOCO decoder-decoder architecture with a recursive inference routine to reuse computation and model state across deeper virtual layers.
Design the recursion to avoid duplicating KV cache entries and to minimize per-step loop overhead, enabling dynamic adjustment of effective depth at test time.
Provide a lightweight control mechanism to scale depth at inference (more steps for harder prompts, fewer for simple ones) without linear memory growth.
impact: YOCO-U lets practitioners cost-effectively scale inference depth to boost reasoning and agentic performance with far lower memory and compute overhead, making adaptive test-time scaling practical in production.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram comparing (a) standard Transformer with growing KV cache vs (b) YOCO-U showing recursive reuse of KV/state.
Flowchart of recursive inference showing a single parameter block being reused across multiple virtual depth steps.
Chart of memory (KV cache) and latency vs. effective depth comparing standard looping, naive depth scaling, and YOCO-U.
Trade-off plot: inference compute vs. reasoning performance (or task accuracy) showing gains from test-time depth scaling with YOCO-U.
paper_title: Universal YOCO for Efficient Depth Scaling
paper_authors: Yutao Sun, Li Dong, Tianzhu Ye, Shaohan Huang, Jianyong Wang
